The compact-stratum argument strengthens measurability by using compact images rather than needing completed measures for arbitrary Borel images. The former source supplies the general mixed-base statement; the latter supplies the matching intrinsic analytic mechanism.

If M=0 the only coupling is zero. If M>0, product couplings normalized to mass M show feasibility, and weak compactness on the product of compact marginal sets gives each smooth strongly convex optimizer. The continuous endpoint membership and weighted-sum identities extend from full output measure to the support, since their conditions are closed.

For each output slice and each fixed endpoint i, the compact base strata D_q partition any compact subset D of the slice support. The preimage of the corresponding image under the endpoint map contains D_q at that output base; the pushforward identity therefore gives the inequality in the required direction. Lipschitz maps in equal dimension send null sets to null sets, so inner regularity and the finite stratum sum imply absolute continuity before the weighted estimate.

The compact images are Borel; the weighted area formula counts each image point at least once. Monotone convergence covers finite but unbounded weights. On a general Borel subset of the slice support, inner regularity bounds its output mass by the integral of the nonnegative Jacobian-weighted function over the subset; testing all such subsets gives the pointwise density comparison even when the right side can have infinite integral.

The finitely many joint strata are measurable. At a density-one point where the maps are differentiable, differentiating their constant base coordinates and the continuous barycenter identity gives D_yF_i=(0,DT_i) and the weighted sum of DT_i equal to I_d. With H the positive definite yy-Hessian block, the pullback product is exactly lambda_i H DT_i. The off-diagonal blocks vanish, and conjugation gives symmetric positive semidefinite C_i with the same determinant and weighted sum I_d.

The pushforward identity places the endpoints in E_i and in the strict positivity sets of f_i for output-almost every point. This transfers to Lebesgue-almost every point where h_p>0. Taking dth roots of the weighted area estimates and then the eigenvalue arithmetic-geometric mean bounds h_p^(1/d) times the stated reciprocal sum by tr(I_d)/d=1. The all-tuples condition then bounds h_p by g; zero-density points need no division. Integrability makes the infinity set of g null, and slice absolute continuity gives it zero output mass.

The fixed domination constraint is closed against nonnegative continuous tests on compact K. Smooth convolution of each finite convex test, plus a vanishing positive quadratic, gives uniform approximation on K. Maximizing each approximant over all couplings places an optimizer in the constrained class, so its objective beats the prescribed old coupling there. Strict separation for a finite family uses nonnegative coefficients because the other set is the whole nonnegative orthant. The finite-intersection property supplies one coupling for all tests.

Integer bases follow from the stated all-allowed-tuples hypothesis, since the exceptional marginal sets are null for every coupling and the integer-base set is closed. The same proof permits a singleton index, n=0, and d=1; it does not use d=0 or claim a physical comparison of different face densities.

dependencies.mapping: Use ambient dimension N=n+d≥1, compact common positive mass marginals and the fixed positive weights. The smooth surplus has the uniform Hessian lower bound; the lemma gives the stated convex-gradient endpoint representation, pushforwards, and barycenter identity.

For each fixed output base p, use Omega=R^d and the smooth map y↦lambda_i grad(phi)(p,y). The supplied V_i are convex C^1 with locally Lipschitz gradients. The lemma gives symmetry and positivity of the exact pullback matrix without needing differentiability of grad(V_i) along the ambient image.

overlap.comparison: Its d≥1 constant-ceiling conclusion is recovered by taking f_i=a_i on K_i and g=(sum_i lambda_i a_i^(-1/d))^(-d) on K. The accepted constant bound neither accommodates unbounded marginal ceilings nor implies domination by a smaller, spatially varying g. Its separate d=0 and sharpness assertions are outside this candidate.
